In females, the third pair of legs left the platform 3.5±0.4 ms (means±s.d., n=35) after the fourth pair, whereas in males it was slightly delayed (3.8±1.8 ms, n=30; Mann–Whitney U=216, P<0.001; Fig. 5; Movie 1).

In both sexes, the fourth pair of legs left the platform close to when peak acceleration occurred (females: 0.4±0.2 ms after peak acceleration, means±s.d., n=35; males: 0.3±0.6 ms before peak acceleration, n=30).
